Serial Resolution: Flagship Mysteries

Decades of reel-to-reel tape copying and cassette circulation left dozens of high-profile radio broadcasts circulating under arbitrary collector labels like "The Part 15", character names, or missing airdates.

Through neural Whisper ASR dialogue transcription on Apple Silicon GPUs, cross-referenced with Jerry Haendiges (jjonez) CBS/NBC master logs, J. David Goldin indices, and contemporaneous newspaper radio grids, we have definitively dated and titled 48 flagship mystery recordings.

1. The Whistler — The 8 "The Part" Tapes Solved

All eight mysterious circulating "The Part" and undated tapes have been identified through on-air announcements, spoken titles, and network time-shift cues:

Original Circulating Filename Spoken Story Title Verified Airdate Key Forensic Evidence
The_Whistler_-_The_Part_15_(Undated).mp3 "Conspiracy" 1948-09-26 Announcer Marvin Miller announces upcoming Oct 3 time change; story of shoe clerk Alvin Peda.
The_Whistler_-_The_Part_16_Unknown.mp3 "Final Decree" 1949-07-24 Gordon Weller & Dr. Perriman canyon hunting shooting; Signal Oil Go-Farther Gasoline billboard.
The_Whistler_-_The_Part_17.mp3 "Incident at Arroyo Grande" 1949-09-25 On-air announcement: "Beginning next Sunday, Oct 2nd, tune in at 7:30." Freight driver Eddie Martin.
The_Whistler_-_The_Part_18.mp3 "Ticket to Murder" 1949-12-18 Kansas City hotel room, recovery of the $30,000 Pyramid Necklace.
The_Whistler_-_The_Part_20.mp3 "The Chinese Elephant Puzzle" 1951-08-26 Singapore diamond smuggling operation inside miniature puzzle boxes to San Francisco gift shop.
The_Whistler_-_The_Part_21_HFC.mp3 "The Professor and the Fox" 1948-02-02 Sponsored by Household Finance Corporation (HFC); estate attorney John Strickland and Mrs. Fremont.
The_Whistler_-_The_Part_22_AFRS.mp3 "Hudson Bay Incident" 1953-05-17 Elliott Bradley and Charles Reeves international mining conference at Hudson Bay hunting lodge.
Whistler_Kaleidoscope_Undated.mp3 "Kaleidoscope" 1944-12-10 Spoken in-character prologue date: "On this midnight of December 10, 1944, the mind of Kit Stratton..."
